newsitem.title: GERMANY: German metal union bristles at idea of wage freeze.
newsitem.headline: German metal union bristles at idea of wage freeze.

text.p: IG Metall, Germany's huge metal and engineering trade union, on Thursday attacked as unreasonable an employer call for a five-year wage freeze in the sector just before the two sides enter key negotiations.

Werner Stumpfe, president of the Gesamtmetall employers federation, had on Wednesday said that a five-year wage freeze would be necessary to restore competitiveness in Germany's metal and engineering sector.
"If Mr Stumpfe is demanding a wage freeze not just for one year but for five years, then he has lost all perspective," IG Metall deputy chairman Walter Riester said in a statement.

Regional negotiations aimed at finding a deal on wages and labour costs are due to start in the steel-making region of North-Rhine Westphalia on Monday, after attempts to secure a nationwide deal failed last month.

IG Metall has indicated it would accept a wage increase in line with inflation next year, but only if accompanied by expenditure to protect employment levels in the sector, where thousands of workers are laid off each month.
The main sticking point in the talks is likely to be sick pay entitlements, which employers are seeking to cut in accordance with a new law that came into effect in October.
Riester denied a suggestion by Stumpfe that workers would be prepared to accept cuts to holiday entitlements in order to maintain sick pay entitlements at the full 100 percent of salary.
